q: Which GooseMode variant means 'ask before every tool call'?
options: Approve
Auto
SmartApprove
Chat
explanation: Auto's strum message is 'Automatically approve tool calls'.
SmartApprove asks only for sensitive calls.
Chat allows no tool calls at all.

q: What do security findings change, relative to permission rules?
options: Security findings feed the judge and can force needs_approval/denied even in Auto mode; permission rules are soft policy
Security findings are advisory logs with no pipeline effect
Security findings only apply in Chat mode
Security findings auto-delete the offending extension
explanation: Findings specifically alter disposition via the judge — not just logs.
Chat mode bypasses tool execution entirely, so findings never surface there.
Deletion is not part of the pipeline; extension lifecycle is separate.

q: What lands in question: after inspection + judging, where does a request in `needs_approval` go next?
options: To the confirmation machinery (ToolConfirmationCoordinator / UI confirm hook), then dispatch or decline
Straight to dispatch, as the judge is advisory
To the security scanner a second time
Nowhere — needs_approval requests are discarded
explanation: needs_approval exists precisely to NOT dispatch silently.
The scanner already ran during inspection.
Decline is a possible outcome, discard never is.

q: When the user rejects a tool call, what does the model receive?
options: A ToolResponse carrying DECLINED_RESPONSE text so the model reacts gracefully
Nothing — the call is silently dropped from the stream
An HTTP 403 error
A cancellation of the whole turn
explanation: Silent drops make the model believe the tool succeeded — the comments on the constants say why that's bad.
The decision is not an HTTP-layer event.
Rejecting one call must not kill the conversation.

q: Why do both Auto and Approve run the same inspectors?
options: Inspectors produce findings for the judge; mode only changes how permission findings are disposed, never whether inspection happens
They don't: Auto skips all inspectors for speed
Inspectors are only for SmartApprove
It's a legacy path bug kept for parity
explanation: Inspection always runs; the disposition is what varies by mode.
SmartApprove consumes findings, but it doesn't own inspection.
It is designed, not a parity accident.

options: Approve tool calls automatically (the default posture), disposal still judge-driven
The model picks its own tools from the registry
Every call is approved AND logged nowhere
Tools run on a different thread pool
explanation: Tool choice is the model's regardless of mode; Auto is about approval.
Telemetry/logging is independent of mode.
Execution is managed uniformly by dispatch.

q: Fix this compile error: a PR makes `inspect_tools` return `Vec<InspectionResult>` directly, but the judge integration fails with a type mismatch. What was the correct contract?
options: Inspection returns per-request findings, not verdicts — the judge must still combine them with GooseMode + rules into PermissionCheckResult
Findings must be converted to strings
The judge must be deleted
Findings must be Option instead of Vec
explanation: The pipeline depends on structured findings, not display strings.
The judge is the verdict stage; deleting it collapses checkpoints 2-3.
Optionality is not the problem — the missing judge step is.
